question: When national energy regulators cannot agree among themselves on how the price-area examination will be carried out, who decides?
reply: {"gold_answers": "yes", "gold_reason": "Article 14(5) of Regulation 2019/943 says that if the regulatory authorities cannot reach a unanimous decision within 3 months, ACER decides within an additional three months on the methodology, assumptions and alternative bidding zone configurations.", "other_articles": [{"doc_id": "reg_2015_1222_art32", "answers": "partially", "why": "Article 32(4)(a) says regulatory authorities may require coordinated amendments within three months. verdict.gold_reason: Article 14(5) of Regulation 2019/943 says that if the regulatory authorities cannot reach a unanimous decision within 3 months, ACER decides within an additional three months on the methodology, assumptions and alternative bidding zone configurations.

other_articles.why: Article 32(4)(a) says regulatory authorities may require coordinated amendments within three months. It names no decision-maker if they disagree, so it does not answer the question.

verdict.ambiguity_reason: 'Price-area examination' is a paraphrase of the bidding zone review. The question is clear enough that Article 14(5) is the intended source.
